newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn seen 1-2 cents lower on Midwest rains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn seen 1-2 cents lower on Midwest rains.

text.p: CBOT corn futures were expected to open one to two cents per bushel lower Monday in response to heavy rains in the central Midwest this weekend, traders said.
"I think the rains are seen as mostly beneficial for corn," said one commission house trader.

However, there is some supportive talk that the week's expected cool temperatures will slow the development of the corn crop, and some traders said there were isolated instances or damage from the weekend rains.
"We're hearing of very isolated damage to the corn," said one trader. "It's very limited, though."
In anticipation of the lower open, some U.S. Midwest grain dealers were taking two to 2.5 cents per bushel protection on corn, and some reported early new-crop sales Monday.
Spillover weakness from Project A was also seen weighing on the market. Overnight, corn was 1-1/4 to two cents per bushel lower.
